claims.statement: A focal small-bowel caliber change with upstream dilation and downstream collapse supports a mechanical obstruction.
claims.limitation: Distribution alone does not establish cause or bowel viability.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected or established small-bowel obstruction.

claims.statement: Presumed adhesive SBO can receive an inpatient nonoperative trial when clinical assessment and CT reveal no peritonitis, strangulation or ischemia.
claims.limitation: Exact clinical application and competing actions require named clinician review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected or established small-bowel obstruction.

claims.statement: A nonoperative SBO trial includes bowel rest, decompression when indicated, intravenous volume and electrolyte replacement, and serial surgical reassessment.
claims.limitation: Exact clinical application and competing actions require named clinician review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected or established small-bowel obstruction.

claims.statement: A closed-loop configuration, especially with reduced mural enhancement or associated fluid, warrants prompt operative assessment for threatened bowel.
claims.limitation: The questions combine anatomy with perfusion findings. A single minor fluid finding is not a universal operation threshold.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected or established small-bowel obstruction.

claims.statement: New peritoneal findings or clinical deterioration during SBO care warrant timely exploration even when earlier assessment supported observation.
claims.limitation: Exact clinical application and competing actions require named clinician review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected or established small-bowel obstruction.

claims.statement: A lactate value in the laboratory reference interval does not exclude bowel ischemia.
claims.limitation: Serial clinical and imaging findings determine concern. No laboratory cutoff is authored.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected or established small-bowel obstruction.

claims.statement: In an adequately performed enteral water-soluble contrast assessment for adhesive SBO, failure to reach the colon by the 24-hour film strongly suggests nonoperative failure.
claims.limitation: Technical adequacy and clinical trajectory matter. This is not an isolated automatic operation deadline.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected or established small-bowel obstruction.

claims.statement: Bologna guidance considers about 72 hours a usual observation period for uncomplicated adhesive SBO, while acknowledging uncertainty about longer observation.
claims.limitation: EAST allows a 3-5 day window or further contrast assessment. No universal maximum or safe waiting rule is asserted. Draft failure combines 72 hours, ongoing symptoms and a failed adequate challenge.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected or established small-bowel obstruction.

claims.statement: Contrast transit predicts the chance of nonoperative resolution and does not override new findings concerning for ischemia or peritonitis.
claims.limitation: Exact clinical application and competing actions require named clinician review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected or established small-bowel obstruction.

claims.statement: Postoperative vomiting and distension can reflect mechanical obstruction or an intra-abdominal complication as well as motility failure, so diagnostic uncertainty requires reassessment.
claims.limitation: A postoperative day by itself does not diagnose benign ileus or mandate exploration.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected or established small-bowel obstruction.

claims.statement: For established postoperative motility dysfunction, supportive care and correction of contributing problems are central while the patient is reassessed for a surgical cause.
claims.limitation: The society guideline principally addresses prevention. Narrative support for established-ileus care is lower certainty. No rescue-drug ranking is asserted.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with postoperative gastrointestinal dysfunction after a recent adequate assessment.

claims.statement: Opioid exposure can contribute to postoperative gastrointestinal hypomotility and supports an opioid-sparing analgesic strategy when feasible.
claims.limitation: Opioid contribution does not independently exclude obstruction or infection.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults after abdominal surgery receiving opioid analgesia.

claims.statement: Absence of prior abdominal surgery does not by itself require exploration in every SBO patient when CT and examination support a supervised nonoperative trial.
claims.limitation: WSES position paper evidence is mostly retrospective. A nonadhesive cause must still be considered.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected or established small-bowel obstruction.

claims.statement: Resolution of SBO in a previously unoperated abdomen does not establish its cause and should be followed by evaluation for an underlying lesion when indicated.
claims.limitation: One adequate retrieved position paper. It does not specify a universal modality, surveillance interval or cancer-screening pathway.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected or established small-bowel obstruction.

claims.statement: Persistent acute abdominal pain with vomiting after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass can warrant early diagnostic laparoscopy despite inconclusive imaging and endoscopy.
claims.limitation: One adequate multisociety guideline. Its recommendation is strong but evidence quality is low. The question requires persistent symptoms after an adequate specialist workup.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with remote Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and persistent acute obstructive symptoms.

claims.statement: Pneumobilia with an ectopic intraluminal stone at a small-bowel transition supports obstruction caused by a migrated biliary stone.
claims.limitation: Case-based literature supports the pattern. Pneumobilia alone is insufficient.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected or established small-bowel obstruction.

claims.statement: Removal of an impacted small-bowel gallstone through enterolithotomy is an obstruction-relieving option when the involved bowel is viable.
claims.limitation: These sources are case reports and narrative discussion. The draft compares the bowel intervention only. One-stage biliary fistula repair is a separate unresolved decision.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected or established small-bowel obstruction.

claims.statement: Nonviable or perforated bowel at a gallstone obstruction may require segmental resection instead of stone extraction with bowel preservation.
claims.limitation: Viability is an operative judgment. No time, color-only rule or quantitative viability cutoff is asserted.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected or established small-bowel obstruction.

claims.statement: Laparoscopic adhesiolysis may suit selected simple adhesive obstructions, while marked distension and complex adhesions increase technical risk.
claims.limitation: Observational selection effects and surgeon experience limit procedure ranking. This teaching point is ranked but unkeyed.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected or established small-bowel obstruction.

claims.statement: Older guidance describes possible therapeutic contrast benefit, while the 2025 trial synthesis does not establish reduced operative intervention from contrast treatment.
claims.limitation: Withhold a scored claim that contrast itself reliably resolves adhesions or prevents surgery. Prognostic transit assessment remains a separate objective.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected or established small-bowel obstruction.

claims.statement: CT can characterize the level and cause of SBO and evaluate findings that influence the need for urgent surgery.
claims.limitation: The draft does not specify an exact postoperative leak-acquisition protocol.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing assessment or management of small-bowel obstruction or postoperative gastrointestinal dysfunction.

claims.statement: Plain abdominal films have limited ability to establish an SBO cause or exclude a complication.
claims.limitation: Serial plain radiography may still answer a defined contrast-progression question.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing assessment or management of small-bowel obstruction or postoperative gastrointestinal dysfunction.

claims.statement: Ultrasound or MRI can be useful in selected SBO assessments when patient constraints or the diagnostic question support them.
claims.limitation: Their use is context-dependent. No universal superiority or numerical accuracy is asserted.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing assessment or management of small-bowel obstruction or postoperative gastrointestinal dysfunction.

claims.statement: Elective colorectal enhanced recovery includes early oral feeding for suitable patients, while persistent symptomatic postoperative dysfunction requires an individualized reassessment.
claims.limitation: Prevention and uncomplicated recovery recommendations do not establish tolerance in a vomiting patient.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing assessment or management of small-bowel obstruction or postoperative gastrointestinal dysfunction.

claims.statement: Adhesiolysis treats an extrinsic adhesive cause of SBO.
claims.limitation: An intraluminal obstruction requires a cause-directed intervention.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing assessment or management of small-bowel obstruction or postoperative gastrointestinal dysfunction.

claims.statement: A lower observed recurrence risk after surgery does not by itself establish an indication for immediate surgery during an otherwise uncomplicated adhesive-SBO episode.
claims.limitation: A current episode still needs a cause and danger assessment. This claim does not decide an elective recurrent-obstruction operation.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults receiving assessment or care for small-bowel obstruction or postoperative gastrointestinal dysfunction.

claims.statement: Intravenous contrast-enhanced CT can assess bowel-wall enhancement when perfusion is a clinical concern in SBO.
claims.limitation: The exact acquisition is chosen for the clinical question. Imaging cannot guarantee exclusion of ischemia and must not delay treatment of clear peritonitis.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults receiving assessment or care for small-bowel obstruction or postoperative gastrointestinal dysfunction.

claims.statement: A new concerning clinical course after an earlier reassuring SBO assessment requires renewed assessment for complications.
claims.limitation: A stable nonperitoneal patient with a new unresolved perfusion question differs from a patient with an established indication for immediate exploration.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults receiving assessment or care for small-bowel obstruction or postoperative gastrointestinal dysfunction.

claims.statement: The recorded postoperative-ileus review does not establish metoclopramide or erythromycin as a reliably effective routine rescue treatment.
claims.limitation: This uncertainty does not rank every analgesic or prokinetic regimen in an individual patient. The attempted regimen-comparison item is parked.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults receiving assessment or care for small-bowel obstruction or postoperative gastrointestinal dysfunction.

claims.statement: A negative CT does not exclude an internal hernia in a symptomatic patient after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass.
claims.limitation: One adequate multisociety guideline synthesizes observational diagnostic evidence. This statement does not by itself rank repeat imaging against exploration or establish a time threshold.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with acute abdominal symptoms after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass.

claims.limitation: WSES position paper evidence is mostly retrospective. A nonadhesive cause must still be considered.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected or established small-bowel obstruction.

claims.statement: Resolution of SBO in a previously unoperated abdomen does not establish its cause and should be followed by evaluation for an underlying lesion when indicated.
claims.limitation: One adequate retrieved position paper. It does not specify a universal modality, surveillance interval or cancer-screening pathway.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected or established small-bowel obstruction.

claims.statement: Persistent acute abdominal pain with vomiting after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass can warrant early diagnostic laparoscopy despite inconclusive imaging and endoscopy.
claims.limitation: One adequate multisociety guideline. Its recommendation is strong but evidence quality is low. The question requires persistent symptoms after an adequate specialist workup.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with remote Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and persistent acute obstructive symptoms.

claims.statement: Pneumobilia with an ectopic intraluminal stone at a small-bowel transition supports obstruction caused by a migrated biliary stone.
claims.limitation: Case-based literature supports the pattern. Pneumobilia alone is insufficient.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected or established small-bowel obstruction.

claims.statement: Removal of an impacted small-bowel gallstone through enterolithotomy is an obstruction-relieving option when the involved bowel is viable.
claims.limitation: These sources are case reports and narrative discussion. The draft compares the bowel intervention only. One-stage biliary fistula repair is a separate unresolved decision.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected or established small-bowel obstruction.

claims.statement: Nonviable or perforated bowel at a gallstone obstruction may require segmental resection instead of stone extraction with bowel preservation.
claims.limitation: Viability is an operative judgment. No time, color-only rule or quantitative viability cutoff is asserted.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected or established small-bowel obstruction.

claims.statement: Laparoscopic adhesiolysis may suit selected simple adhesive obstructions, while marked distension and complex adhesions increase technical risk.
claims.limitation: Observational selection effects and surgeon experience limit procedure ranking. This teaching point is ranked but unkeyed.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected or established small-bowel obstruction.

claims.statement: Older guidance describes possible therapeutic contrast benefit, while the 2025 trial synthesis does not establish reduced operative intervention from contrast treatment.
claims.limitation: Withhold a scored claim that contrast itself reliably resolves adhesions or prevents surgery. Prognostic transit assessment remains a separate objective.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with suspected or established small-bowel obstruction.

claims.statement: CT can characterize the level and cause of SBO and evaluate findings that influence the need for urgent surgery.
claims.limitation: The draft does not specify an exact postoperative leak-acquisition protocol.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing assessment or management of small-bowel obstruction or postoperative gastrointestinal dysfunction.

claims.statement: Plain abdominal films have limited ability to establish an SBO cause or exclude a complication.
claims.limitation: Serial plain radiography may still answer a defined contrast-progression question.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing assessment or management of small-bowel obstruction or postoperative gastrointestinal dysfunction.

claims.statement: Ultrasound or MRI can be useful in selected SBO assessments when patient constraints or the diagnostic question support them.
claims.limitation: Their use is context-dependent. No universal superiority or numerical accuracy is asserted.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing assessment or management of small-bowel obstruction or postoperative gastrointestinal dysfunction.

claims.statement: Elective colorectal enhanced recovery includes early oral feeding for suitable patients, while persistent symptomatic postoperative dysfunction requires an individualized reassessment.
claims.limitation: Prevention and uncomplicated recovery recommendations do not establish tolerance in a vomiting patient.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing assessment or management of small-bowel obstruction or postoperative gastrointestinal dysfunction.

claims.statement: Adhesiolysis treats an extrinsic adhesive cause of SBO.
claims.limitation: An intraluminal obstruction requires a cause-directed intervention.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing assessment or management of small-bowel obstruction or postoperative gastrointestinal dysfunction.

revisionResearch.retainedClaimPolicy: The original 25 atomic claims and their dates are preserved. The retained original source records and mappings are stored under independentReviewRound1.
revisionResearch.verification: Bologna recurrence and observation limits, EAST CT danger findings, the corrected OBA persistent-symptom recommendation and the contemporary CT-perfusion discussion were targeted online. Other reused claims retain their original checks.
revisionResearch.acrAccess: Both official ACR narrative routes again returned 403. Search-result text was excluded as evidence. ACR terms were inspected for targeted factual/copyright boundaries.
revisionResearch.rightsBoundary: The added CC BY-NC publication supplies one independently synthesized factual cross-check in the internal authoring packet. No source expression is redistributed.

finalAtomicClaimCheck.use: Targeted verification of the negative-CT limitation. No diagnostic probability or timing rule is extracted; no source text is stored.

salvageComposition.meaning: Unchanged exact PASS question and node; case composition only.
